hotspot_events.title: Aluminum squeeze nears Nov 18 expiry
hotspot_events.heat_reason: November contracts' combined open interest exceeds the exchange's entire inventory; LME inventory is the lowest since 1990, spot premium the widest in 36 years, and the Nov 18 expiry and delivery are imminent - aluminum fin and extrusion costs and lead times are under pressure together
hotspot_events.summary: LME 3M official settlement on Nov 13: USD 3,018/ton; spot at USD 3,150.50/ton. Spot premium hit USD 176.80/ton intraday on Nov 12 - still the widest in 36 years - and the official settlement spread on Nov 13 was USD 132.50/ton. LME inventory is 224,150 tons (lowest since 1990, down over 50% this year), 99.98% of Russian origin, with a single holder accounting for 30-39% of warrants. Combined November contract open interest exceeds the exchange's entire inventory; four undisclosed longs together hold at least 25% of open interest, and if the dominant position's share rises further the LME may trigger its forced-lending rules. November contracts expire Nov 18 (Wednesday).

hotspot_events.title: Transformer / switchgear lead times stretch to 90-160 weeks as the AI bottleneck shifts to power and building delivery
hotspot_events.heat_reason: Substation transformer lead times are 90-160 weeks and medium-voltage switchgear 52-80 weeks; Cerebras confirms the AI delivery bottleneck has shifted from chips to land, power and buildings, and procurement of power-distribution equipment for data centers and HVAC projects is under pressure together
hotspot_events.summary: In the Phoenix, Arizona market, medium-voltage switchgear lead times are 52-80 weeks, standard pad-mount transformers 40-65 weeks, and extra-large substation transformers 90-160 weeks (even approved projects may wait 2-3 years for power), with structural steel lead times doubling to 55 weeks. Cerebras said on Nov 12 that first deliveries under its 750MW take-or-pay contract with OpenAI are delayed because of land, power and data-center building construction (not chips), with delivery pace expected to recover in H2 2027.
numbers: Structural steel lead times doubled to 55 weeks

industry_updates.title: Samsung in talks to buy Modine (rumored, unconfirmed)
industry_updates.detail: Bloomberg reported on Nov 12 that Samsung Electronics is in talks to acquire US data-center cooling firm Modine; a deal could be reached within weeks or could fall through. Samsung said it could not confirm, and Modine declined to comment. Modine rose about 29% after hours on Nov 12 and about 28-33% intraday on Nov 13 to around USD 137. Modine is scheduled to hold an analyst and investor day on Nov 18.

industry_updates.title: LG's USD 64 million Virginia HVAC assembly plant
industry_updates.detail: LG Electronics plans to invest USD 64 million in a new HVAC equipment assembly plant in Isle of Wight County, Virginia, expanding US commercial climate-technology capacity. Headcount, construction timeline and production start date are pending official confirmation.

industry_updates.title: Tongfei private placement lands (net proceeds RMB 889 million)
industry_updates.detail: On Nov 12, Tongfei's board approved using the placement proceeds to inject RMB 70 million of paid-in capital into its wholly owned subsidiary Suzhou Tongfei Temperature Control and provide an interest-free loan of RMB 397.9114 million, funding the southern headquarters and industrial cooling equipment and components project. Net proceeds from this private placement were RMB 889 million.

industry_updates.title: Trane at the Nov 12 Baird conference: USD 12.5 billion order backlog
industry_updates.detail: The CEO said 11 of 14 North American commercial HVAC vertical markets grew in Q3. The order backlog is USD 12.5 billion (all signed purchase orders). Thermo King Q3 orders rose more than 30% YoY (ending a four-year decline). Applied capacity has expanded 4x in three years. Supply pressure is expected to ease within 6-9 months as suppliers expand capacity. No 2027 guidance was given, pending the Q4 earnings report.

industry_updates.title: Daikin D60-W 60MW AI factory cooling reference architecture (backfill)
industry_updates.detail: Daikin Applied released the D60-W 60MW AI factory cooling reference architecture on Nov 10 (built on the NVIDIA DSX AI Factory platform + Vera Rubin NVL72), with 6 deployable units supporting 60MW of IT load - 92% liquid-cooled, 8% air-cooled - centered on the Magnitude WME oil-free magnetic-bearing centrifugal chiller (up to 10MW per unit). Its in-house CDU and data-center dry coolers are still under development, targeted for H2 2027.

industry_updates.title: Lenovo's new ThinkSystem servers (Neptune liquid cooling)
industry_updates.detail: Lenovo launched new ThinkSystem servers powered by AMD EPYC processors around Nov 12, with Neptune liquid-cooling technology and AI factory expansion services. A board meeting is scheduled for Nov 19 to review interim results and consider an interim dividend.

siphon_effects.detail: DDR4 spot weekly average USD 46.51 (down 2.7% WoW, fourth straight weekly decline); the single-day session average on Nov 12 was USD 44.714. In the US DRAM antitrust suit, a judge on Nov 14 denied motions to dismiss by Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron; the three must file answers by Dec 7. TrendForce expects Q4 PC DRAM contract prices to rise another 13%-18% QoQ, and CFM forecasts mobile memory could rise more than 20% in Q1 2027. SK Hynix says the shortage will last at least until 2030.

No new price-hike announcements in the window: Samsung Electro-Mechanics' Q4 hike remains at the Nov 2 terms (consumer-grade X5R up about 25-30%, AI-server X6S up 10-20%, TrendForce estimates, not company-confirmed); Yageo's next round of high-capacitance hikes of over +50% remains distributor-sourced and unconfirmed; Fenghua said in a Nov 6 investor briefing that product prices are rising steadily but gave no specific increases or effective dates; KEMET's second-round hike took effect Nov 1 (T520/T521/T530 series up 20-30%); industrial-grade aluminum electrolytic 400-450V lead times are 18-22 weeks.

LME 3M official settlement on Nov 13: USD 13,545/ton, breaking below USD 13,500 intraday to a roughly 4-month low and heading for a fifth straight weekly decline. SHFE copper spot premium averaged RMB 275/ton on Nov 13 (down RMB 500 in a day). The Yangshan premium hit a fresh record of USD 285/ton. SHFE inventory is 27,642 tons (lowest since December 2023). The 2611 contract's last trading day is Nov 16, with delivery on Nov 17-18.

LME 3M official settlement on Nov 13: USD 3,018/ton; spot USD 3,150.50/ton. Spot premium hit USD 176.80/ton intraday on Nov 12 (widest in 36 years). LME inventory is 224,150 tons (lowest since 1990). Combined November contract open interest exceeds total inventory, and four undisclosed longs together hold at least 25% of open interest. November contracts expire Nov 18.

The Panasonic Hukou (Hsinchu, Taiwan) fire still has no new resumption or investigation updates as of Nov 13/16 (Nov 10 terms: production lines remain halted; resumption requires repairs, equipment reset and customer requalification, often taking months). November electronic-cloth prices continue to rise (7628 electronic cloth at RMB 14.4-14.8/m). Jin'an Guoji announced on Nov 9 an investment of about RMB 500 million in a new electronic-grade glass-fiber cloth project with annual capacity of 130 million meters in Ningguo, Anhui, planned to start production in March 2027. High-performance CCL procurement cycles are 24-32 weeks.

Infineon said on its Nov 10 earnings call that lead times continue to lengthen and supply is tightening, with high-performance SiC and high-power modules seeing supply tightness. FY2027 revenue guidance is about EUR 20 billion, with data-center power revenue expected near EUR 4 billion. ST's fourth price hike (effective 2027-01-01) remains an online-circulated letter; TrendForce said on Nov 12 that the product scope and increases are unconfirmed. No new onsemi news in the window.

siphon_effects.material: Liquid cooling / CDU and high-density power distribution
siphon_effects.detail: CoreWeave's Q3 capex was USD 14.511 billion in a single quarter, with full-year capex guidance raised to USD 37-39 billion; power in operation exceeds 1.7GW and contracted power exceeds 4.6GW. Cerebras' Q3 core revenue was USD 231 million (up 70% YoY), but first deliveries under the 750MW OpenAI contract are delayed (land, power and building construction - not chips), with recovery expected in H2 2027. Nvidia reports Q3 earnings after the bell on Nov 17 (company guidance: USD 108 billion +/-2%).

cross_industry.detail: Nucor plans to raise plate prices by USD 70/short ton on Nov 13 and open its December order book at the same time; orders must be submitted by Nov 27. SMU's plate average was USD 1,550/short ton as of Nov 10 (up USD 55 WoW); hot-rolled coil averaged USD 1,375/short ton (up USD 25 WoW). Mill lead times are 3-5 weeks. As of Nov 14/15, no other mills had followed.

CAAM: October NEV production / sales were 2.017 million / 1.94 million units (up 13.8% / 13.1% YoY), with NEVs accounting for 64.3% of new-car sales. October auto exports were 1.066 million units (up 60.2% YoY), including 606,000 NEVs (up 1.4x YoY). CPCA data: October domestic retail sales of NEV passenger cars were 1.109 million units (down 13.7% YoY, the 10th straight monthly decline). September power-battery installations were 87.2GWh (up 14.7% YoY).

Transformer and switchgear lead times - see top story 3 (medium-voltage switchgear 52-80 weeks, pad-mount transformers 40-65 weeks, substation transformers 90-160 weeks). China's transformer exports reached RMB 64.6 billion in 2025 (up 36% YoY), with lead times of 10-12 months. Eaton disclosed data-center-related orders up 240% YoY.

Newly installed solar capacity in Q3 was about 38.76GW (up 38% YoY); January-September cumulative additions were 110.83GW. N-type dense polysilicon averaged RMB 40.5/kg in the week of Nov 13 (production cost RMB 42.8/kg - a loss of RMB 2.3/kg); October output was 105,100 tons (down 7.81% MoM), with November scheduled output expected at 82,200 tons (down 21.79% MoM). The 15% US Section 232 tariff on polysilicon takes effect Dec 4.

ABB's robotics-business sale was vetoed by China; the CEO said on Nov 13 that SoftBank is leading efforts to secure approval. Schneider's acquisition of PTC goes to a shareholder vote on Dec 17 (Swiss Financial Time, Nov 13; ad-hoc-news, Nov 15).
No new letters in this window (INVT's Oct 8 adjustment and Kehua Data's Nov 1 adjustment were already reported).

Medium-voltage switchgear lead times are 52-80 weeks, standard pad-mount transformers 40-65 weeks, and extra-large substation transformers 90-160 weeks (even approved projects may wait 2-3 years for power); structural steel lead times doubled to 55 weeks. China's transformer exports reached RMB 64.6 billion in 2025 (up 36% YoY), with lead times of 10-12 months (AZ Big Media, citing LGE report, Nov 14).

Dense price hikes in December-January: Insulfoam +5% from Dec 1, Rockwool +6% from Jan 1, Owens Corning +6% for building insulation / +8% for mechanical and pipe insulation from Jan 4 (one product line +12%), Johns Manville +5%-12% from Jan 11, Knauf +6%-10% from Jan 22, Manson +6%-10% from Feb 1, AGM Industries +7.5%-10% from Dec 1 (ContractorPlus, Nov 3; General Insulation, Nov 2).

Sherwin-Williams' Paint Stores Group raised prices 8% from September (against high-single-digit raw-material inflation). Perstorp raised global polyol prices from Nov 1 (Penta +EUR 100/ton). Eastman announced on Oct 31 that ester spot prices would rise USD 0.06/lb in North and Latin America from Nov 1 (Tickeron; Xecss, citing Perstorp's announcement).

Apollo valves rise 4%-8% from Dec 1, and VSH press fittings +3%-4%. UK-based Pressure Tech raised all product prices 5% from Nov 1 (citing steel safeguard measures and higher oil and electricity prices) (ContractorPlus, Nov 3; Pressure Tech notice email).

This round (batch 1) covered 11 subcategories: 4 substantive hits (coatings, insulation / soundproofing materials, valves, transformers & instrument transformers - see the corresponding entries), 1 under mild pressure (Digital Logic: VersaLogic's Nov 4 briefing said some single-source components had no vendor lead-time commitments for weeks, with several delivery commitments pushed back over a month), and the other 6 (Access Control Panels, Cell Battery, Fire Detectors, Hoses, Pin Or Rivet, Uncategorized Access Control) with no anomalies. Cell Battery: LFP cell prices edged down slightly (100Ah at RMB 0.408/Wh, down 1.2% WoW), with no shortage signals.
No price-hike / lead-time news for the 5 compressor types (centrifugal / reciprocating / rotary / scroll / screw) in this window.

No new Sanhua announcements; DunAn received a utility-model patent authorization for an electronic expansion valve on Nov 13 (CN224970274U); Yinlun's Nov 13 share-price drop of 5.01% was market movement, with no product news.
